body.statement: In a dominated differentiable statistical model, if the real parameter \(\theta\) is pathwise differentiable at \(P\in\mathcal P_4^{\circ}\) with canonical gradient \(D\in L_0^2(P)\), then the limit distribution of every regular estimator is the convolution of \(N(0,E_P[D(O)^2])\) and another probability law.  In particular, whenever its asymptotic variance exists, it is at least \(V_P=E_P[D(O)^2]\).

source.verbatim_statement: Suppose that the sequence of experiments is locally asymptotically normal and that the estimator sequence is regular. Then its limit distribution is the convolution of the efficient normal distribution and another probability distribution.

attestation.note: Transcribed from van der Vaart (1998), Theorem 25.20, and specialized in the node statement to the scalar canonical gradient.
